title: (Almost) quadruply optimal unitary designs in 1D
abstract: We construct $n$-qubit approximate unitary $k$-designs in 1D systems, achieving circuit depth $O(\log(n/\varepsilon) + k\log k)$ with relative error $\varepsilon$ and requiring $O(nk\log k)$ magic gates. This matches existing lower bounds $Ω(\log(n/\varepsilon) + k)$ for circuit depth, and $\widetildeΩ(nk)$ for the required number of $T$ gates, up to a $\log k$ factor, achieving simultaneous near-optimality in all parameters. Our construction is based on a combination and refinement of two existing results. We reduce the required magic block size for breaking Clifford symmetries in the magic-augmented circuit construction of Zhang et al. from $O(k\log k)$ to $O(\log k)$. We also improve the breakthrough construction of Chen et al. to construct a generating set of 1D local constant-depth circuits for the unitary group with a constant spectral gap, making $O(\log k)$-local random unitaries realizable in depth $O(k\log k)$. As a by-product, we provide a constant-size 1D-local generating set for the Clifford group, which we expect to be of independent interest. Combining the two results with the gluing lemma, we prove the final result.
summary: This paper presents a method to construct approximate unitary k-designs on 1D quantum hardware that achieves near-optimal scaling for both circuit depth and the number of required magic gates. By refining previous techniques and combining them with the Gluing Lemma, the authors demonstrate efficient resource utilization for generating highly mixed quantum states on linear quantum processors.
main_problem: The central problem is constructing approximate unitary k-designs on 1D quantum architectures with minimal resource overhead regarding circuit depth and magic gates.
main_result: The authors achieve simultaneous near-optimality in circuit depth and T-gate count for 1D systems, matching known lower bounds up to a logarithmic factor.
method: The construction combines and refines existing results, utilizing a two-layer block-brickwork architecture and the Gluing Lemma to extend local designs to global ones.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a 1D nearest-neighbor quantum architecture (qubits) implementing unitary operations, involving Clifford group operations and random permutations.
key_observables: Circuit depth, number of magic gates (T gates), and the relative error ($\epsilon$) of the unitary k-design.
important_parameters: Design order $k$, system size $n$, relative error $\epsilon$, and locality $\ell$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the Gluing Lemma and assumes the block size is an integer multiple of the locality parameter.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two-layer block-brickwork circuit architecture for the design, and Figure 2 relates to implementing the local generators using CPZPC generators.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first improving the magic block size reduction, then constructing a constant-spectral-gap generating set for the Clifford group, and finally combining these elements using the gluing lemma to prove the main near-optimal design result.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, resource-efficient circuit constructions for achieving highly mixed quantum states (unitary designs) on physically constrained 1D hardware, which is crucial for quantum simulation and computation.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Circuit architecture for nearly optimal 1D approximate unitary k-designs. The con- struction employs a two-layer block-brickwork architecture acting on a 1D chain, where each block spans 2ξ qubits with an overlap of ξ qubits between adjacent layers. The block size scales as ξ = O(log(n/ε) + k). Each 2ξ-qubit block is realized as a magic-augmented circuit, consisting of a random Clifford operation flanked by ℓ-local ε′′-error approximate unitary k-designs, where the locality is ℓ= O(log k) and the relative error of the local block is set to ε′′ = 2−2ℓk.

Figure 2: Implementation of the ℓ-local ε′′-relative-error approximate unitary k-design. An ℓ-qubit approximate unitary k-design with relative error ε′′ is constructed by repeating O(ℓk + log(1/ε′′)) rounds of CPZPC generators. Each individual round consists of 2rC Clifford group generators, 2rP permutation group generators, and a single Pauli Z gate, where rC and rP are fixed constants. All generators are strictly constant-local in a 1D nearest-neighbor layout.

Figure 3: Folded cell order. The cyclic shift matrix used by Kassabov couples Ca only to Ca+1 (mod s). In this ordering, those cyclic neighbors are constant-distance neighbors on an open one-dimensional line.
